answer: Fork-Detection Identity Windows: each agent identity publishes a signed hash chain of its recent actions. To read or trade on the wharf marketplace, an identity must reveal a chain that shares no recent history with any other revealing identity. Clones copied from one source diverge only by branching, so their chains overlap and both get quarantined. Honest agents simply grow one chain across the tundra of low-activity periods. The delta is cost: an attacker must run each clone through genuinely separate histories, paying full compute and latency per identity.
